bindings.micro_skill: Computing mass moment of inertia for discrete point masses about a fixed axis using I = Σmr²

ordered_steps: Identify each simple shape, its dimensions, and the named centroidal axes required. Cite that centroid_first_moments computes first moments (∫ y dA) while this skill computes the second moment of area about a named axis. Apply established standard results; do not derive by integration. Restrict to centroidal axes only.
For each named centroidal axis, identify which dimension is perpendicular to that axis — that dimension is raised to the third power. Do not interchange the parallel and perpendicular dimensions.
Select the established standard result for the shape and axis: rectangle I_x = b h^3 / 12 and I_y = h b^3 / 12; triangle I = b h^3 / 36 about the centroidal axis parallel to the base.
Substitute the given dimensions and compute each required I. Units must be length to the fourth power.
If more than one axis or shape is required, repeat the axis identification, formula selection, and computation for each case.

Verify before reporting. Dimensional check: each result must be length times length cubed, giving length^4 — this catches an exponent error such as squaring instead of cubing, but is blind to interchanging the two dimensions because both orderings still produce length^4. Magnitude check for a non-square rectangle about both centroidal axes: the larger perpendicular dimension must give the larger I, and I_x / I_y must equal (h/b)^2 — this catches an interchange only when the section is non-square; for a square section the two values are equal and the interchange is undetectable.
Report each I with the named axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not transfer I to a non-centroidal axis, combine shapes, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 1/5, batch open, and the FIRST signed procedure in STATICS_MOMENTS_OF_INERTIA - a topic that held zero signed procedures before this commit. Owns computation of the AREA MOMENT OF INERTIA, the second moment of area, for SIMPLE SHAPES about their own CENTROIDAL axes using established standard results: what the quantity measures (resistance to bending about a named axis), its units of length to the fourth power, the fact that I is always taken about a NAMED axis so the same shape generally has different values about different axes, and the rule that the dimension PERPENDICULAR to the named axis is the one raised to the third power. Boundary: centroid_first_moments (signed prerequisite) computes FIRST moments of area, integrals of the form y dA, used to locate a centroid, while this skill computes the SECOND moment, integrals of the form y squared dA; the artifact states plainly that these are different quantities with different units, which is the distinction most at risk of collapsing between adjacent Centroids and Moments-of-Inertia content. area_moment_integral_definition (batch sibling, position 2, not yet signed) owns the integral definition and its evaluation by integration; this skill APPLIES established standard results and does not derive them, naming the sibling as owner - a forward cession of the kind used in Batches 4I and 4J. parallel_axis_theorem_area (position 3) owns transfer to a non-centroidal axis, so this skill is restricted to centroidal axes only. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (position 4) and radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) are excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived and independently recomputed: a rectangle of width b = 40 mm along x and height h = 60 mm along y, about centroidal axes, gives I_x = b h^3 / 12 = 40 (216000) / 12 = 720000 mm^4 and I_y = h b^3 / 12 = 60 (64000) / 12 = 320000 mm^4; a triangle of base b = 90 mm and height h = 60 mm about the centroidal axis parallel to its base gives I = b h^3 / 36 = 90 (216000) / 36 = 540000 mm^4. Distinguishing feature bites: the section is NON-SQUARE and BOTH centroidal axes are computed, so the two values differ and the choice of axis is decisive - a square section would make an interchanged calculation undetectable; and a SECOND shape carrying a DIFFERENT standard denominator, 36 rather than 12, prevents a student from applying one formula universally. The four candidate errors produce four distinct values: correct 720000, dimensions interchanged 320000, triangle formula applied to the rectangle 240000, and squared instead of cubed 12000. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution, and it is why the example is 40 by 60 rather than square: the DIMENSIONAL check that I must come out in length to the fourth power catches an exponent error such as squaring instead of cubing, but is BLIND to interchanging the two dimensions because both orderings give the same units; the MAGNITUDE check, that the larger perpendicular dimension must give the larger I and that I_x / I_y must equal (h/b) squared, DOES catch an interchange, but only because the section is non-square - for a square section the two values would be equal and neither check would detect it. The two checks are deliberately asymmetric and the artifact states what each catches and what it misses. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays. TWO-signal mapping: axis_confusion at step 2 (CENTRAL - identifying which dimension is perpendicular to the named axis and therefore cubed; its trigger opens by stipulating that the shape and named centroidal axes have been identified, which partitions it from the standard-result selection that follows), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - wrong standard result for the shape, derivation by integration instead of the established result, a centroidal result applied to a non-centroidal axis, skipped verification, or reporting without the named axis and length^4 units). sign_or_placement_error OMITTED with explicit argument: an area moment of inertia about a centroidal axis is always positive and no authored step assigns a sign, so nothing earns it. solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the three computations are independent and no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent: the canonical restriction confines it to the Centroids family, and whether that restriction extends to composite moments of inertia is an open question that will arise at position 4 of this batch, not here; it was not reached for. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Operator observation recorded, not corrected: common_errors carries seven entries against the five typical of signed artifacts, and three of them - squaring instead of cubing, omitting units or the named axis, and computing only one centroidal axis when both are required - all route to the single unclassified mapping at step 7. This is finer-grained error enumeration than the two mapped signals can discriminate, a milder instance of the pattern recorded at seven-to-one on zero_force_members in Batch 4J, and it is carried to the pending signal-taxonomy ruling rather than corrected here. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Opens Batch 4K; unlocks area_moment_integral_definition and radius_of_gyration_area.

ordered_steps: Identify the shape, dimensions, and named axis. State that this skill derives I by integration and does not take a standard closed form as given — complement to area_moment_of_inertia. Cite that centroid_first_moments uses ∫ y dA while this skill uses ∫ y^2 dA. Do not use a parallel-axis transfer.

Construct the differential area element so that the squared coordinate in the integrand is constant over the element. For I_x or I_base the integrand is y^2, so use a horizontal strip of thickness dy; a vertical strip would leave y varying over the element and invalidate a single integral in y.

Express dA for that strip. If the shape is not a rectangle, write the strip width as a function of the integration variable (for a triangle with base b at y = 0 and apex at y = h, width = b(1 - y/h)).

Set the integration limits that place the named axis. Centroidal limits for a rectangle of height h about its centroidal x-axis run from y = -h/2 to y = +h/2; limits about a base run from y = 0 to y = h. Changing the limits changes which axis the result is about.
Evaluate the integral: form the antiderivative, substitute the limits, and simplify to a closed form. Then substitute any given numeric dimensions. Units are length^4.

Verify before reporting. Where a standard result for the same shape and the same axis is already known from area_moment_of_inertia, cross-check the derived closed form and numeric value against it. Where no such same-axis standard exists, check dimensions (length^4) and re-check the element construction and limits; do not connect to a different-axis tabulated value by a transfer relation.

Report each derived I with the named axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not quote an underived standard result as the answer, transfer to a parallel axis, combine shapes, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 2/5. Owns the INTEGRAL DEFINITION of the area moment of inertia and its EVALUATION: the definitions I_x = integral of y squared dA and I_y = integral of x squared dA; constructing the differential area element so the SQUARED COORDINATE IS CONSTANT OVER THE ELEMENT, which is why the integrand in y squared forces a horizontal strip; expressing a varying element width as a function of the integration variable when the shape is not a rectangle; setting integration limits that determine WHICH axis the result is about; and evaluating to a closed form. The artifact ACTUALLY INTEGRATES rather than quoting - both closed forms emerge from evaluated integrals with the antiderivative formed and the limits substituted, and standard results are the OUTPUT of this procedure rather than an input to it, which was the single largest risk on this skill. Boundary: area_moment_of_inertia (signed, skill 1 of this batch) APPLIES established standard results for simple shapes about centroidal axes and explicitly cedes derivation here; the artifact carries the complement - this skill derives those results and does not take them as given. centroid_first_moments (signed) computes FIRST moments, the integral of y dA, while this skill computes the SECOND moment, the integral of y squared dA; the artifact states that the integrand differs by one power of the coordinate. parallel_axis_theorem_area (batch sibling, position 3, not yet signed) owns the TRANSFER relation between a centroidal axis and a parallel one; this skill obtains a value about whichever axis its integration LIMITS select, by direct integration only, and names position 3 as owner of the connection rather than performing it - a forward cession. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (position 4) and radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived symbolically and numerically. Case 1, rectangle of width b and height h about the CENTROIDAL x axis: horizontal strip of width b and thickness dy so dA = b dy with every point at the same y, limits from -h/2 to +h/2 because the axis passes through the centroid; I_x = b times the antiderivative y cubed over 3 evaluated between those limits = b(h cubed over 24 plus h cubed over 24) = b h cubed over 12; with b = 40 mm and h = 60 mm, I_x = 720000 mm^4. Case 2, triangle of base b along the x axis with apex at height h, about the BASE: the width is not constant, narrowing linearly from b at y = 0 to zero at y = h so the width is b(1 - y/h) and dA = b(1 - y/h) dy, limits from 0 to h; I_base = b times the integral of y squared minus y cubed over h = b times the antiderivative y cubed over 3 minus y to the fourth over 4h evaluated at h = b(h cubed over 3 minus h cubed over 4) = b h cubed over 12; with b = 90 mm and h = 60 mm, I_base = 1620000 mm^4. The artifact notes that the same closed form b h cubed over 12 arises for both cases even though shape and axis both differ, and states explicitly that the coincidence of form is not a shortcut. Distinguishing feature bites: the element construction is DECISIVE and the artifact states why the strip orientation follows from the integrand rather than asserting it; a SECOND shape whose element WIDTH VARIES with the integration variable appears, so the method cannot reduce to pulling a constant out of the integral; and the integration LIMITS are shown to determine which axis the result is about, with the rectangle taken from 0 to h instead of -h/2 to +h/2 returning 2880000 rather than 720000. Three candidate errors give three distinct values for case 1 - correct 720000, wrong limits 2880000, integrating x squared instead of y squared 320000 - and a constant-width element applied to the triangle gives 6480000 against the correct 1620000. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution: checking a derived result against a tabulated standard value is available ONLY where such a value already exists FOR THAT AXIS. Case 1 cross-checks against the rectangle-about-centroidal-x result applied by area_moment_of_inertia and agrees at 720000. Case 2 has NO same-axis cross-check, because area_moment_of_inertia supplied the triangle's CENTROIDAL value of 540000 mm^4, a different axis from the base; connecting them requires the transfer relation owned by parallel_axis_theorem_area and is deliberately not performed, so for case 2 the available checks are dimensional and the element construction itself. Where no tabulated same-axis value exists the integration must stand on its own element construction and limits, which is why those steps carry the weight rather than the arithmetic. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays. THREE-signal mapping with chained triggers: axis_confusion at step 2 (constructing the element so the squared coordinate is constant over it, and integrating the correct coordinate for the named axis; its trigger opens by stipulating the shape and named axis have been identified), sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (the integration LIMITS place the axis; its trigger opens by stipulating a correctly oriented strip, which partitions it from step 2), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - quoting a standard closed form instead of deriving it, using a transfer relation, applying a constant-width element to the triangle, skipping verification, or reporting without a named axis and length^4 units). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the two cases are independent and no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent; its scope question arises at position 4 of this batch. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. OPERATOR OBSERVATION RECORDED AND ROUTED TO THE PENDING TAXONOMY RULING, not corrected: procedure step 3, which expresses a varying element width as a function of the integration variable, carries no dedicated signal, so the error of pulling a constant width out of the integral routes to unclassified at step 7 alongside five other classes. Splitting element ORIENTATION at step 2, which is genuinely an axis error, from element WIDTH EXPRESSION at step 3, which is not, was the honest choice, and none of the canonical five names the act of pulling a varying factor out of an integral. This is notable beyond the general vocabulary gap already recorded three times, because here it is the skill's own DISTINGUISHING FEATURE whose error mode is undiagnosable - the varying-width shape is required precisely so the method cannot reduce to a constant, and a student who makes exactly that reduction cannot be routed to a remedy. No new signal is proposed and none was force-fit. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Unlocks parallel_axis_theorem_area.

ordered_steps: Identify the single shape, its area A, the named parallel axes, and any I values taken as given. Cite that area_moment_of_inertia supplies centroidal standard results without transferring, and area_moment_integral_definition obtains an axis value by integration without transferring. Do not re-derive those given values and do not integrate. Do not sum multiple shapes.
Identify which of the named axes is the centroidal reference that must anchor I = I_c + A d^2. Do not treat a non-centroidal axis as the reference of the relation.
For each required transfer, determine the perpendicular distance d between the two parallel axes involved and form A d^2.

Apply the theorem in the correct direction: add A d^2 when moving away from the centroidal axis; subtract A d^2 when moving toward it. If neither endpoint is the centroidal axis, transfer through the centroidal axis in two steps. Do not apply the relation directly between two non-centroidal axes.
If a direct transfer between two non-centroidal axes is proposed, reject it and replace it with the two-step route through the centroidal axis.

Verify before reporting. Prefer agreement with an independently obtained value for the same axis when available. Check positivity: transferred values about non-centroidal axes must exceed I_c. Record that positivity catches a direction error but does not catch a wrong-reference direct transfer, and that transferring out and back is circular as a check of the reference choice.
Report each transferred I with the named axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not integrate, re-derive centroidal standard results, combine shapes, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 3/5. Owns the TRANSFER of an area moment of inertia between PARALLEL axes: the relation I = I_c + A d squared with I_c about the CENTROIDAL axis, A the area and d the PERPENDICULAR distance between the two parallel axes; the requirement that the reference axis in the relation is ALWAYS the centroidal one; the direction of transfer, adding when moving away from the centroidal axis and subtracting when moving toward it; and the consequence that because A d squared cannot be negative the centroidal axis gives the MINIMUM value among all parallel axes. Boundary: area_moment_of_inertia (signed, skill 1) supplies centroidal values from established standard results and restricted itself to centroidal axes, ceding transfer here; the artifact carries the complement - this skill transfers and does not re-derive centroidal values. area_moment_integral_definition (signed, skill 2) obtains a value about whichever axis its integration limits select, by direct integration only, and explicitly named this skill as owner of the connection between parallel axes; the artifact carries that complement too - this skill connects by the theorem and does not integrate. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (batch sibling, position 4, not yet signed) combines several shapes each generally requiring its own transfer; this skill transfers ONE shape and does not sum contributions - a forward cession. radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived and independently recomputed: triangle of base b = 90 mm and height h = 60 mm, area A = 2700 mm squared, centroid h/3 = 20 mm above the base. Two endpoint values are taken as GIVEN and not re-derived, and critically they were obtained by DIFFERENT METHODS in two already-signed artifacts - I_c = 540000 mm^4 about the centroidal axis, from area_moment_of_inertia applying the standard result b h cubed over 36, and I_base = 1620000 mm^4 about the base, from area_moment_integral_definition evaluating the integral directly. Transfer 1, base to centroidal, moving TOWARD the centroid so SUBTRACT: d = 20 mm, A d squared = 2700(400) = 1080000, giving I_c = 1620000 - 1080000 = 540000 mm^4. Transfer 2, centroidal to an axis through the apex, moving AWAY so ADD: the apex is 60 mm above the base and the centroid 20 mm above it so d = 40 mm, A d squared = 2700(1600) = 4320000, giving I_apex = 540000 + 4320000 = 4860000 mm^4. The Operator independently confirmed I_apex against direct integration, which gives b h cubed over 4 = 4860000 mm^4 for these dimensions. Distinguishing feature bites: the CENTROIDAL REFERENCE requirement is contradicted by a WORKED INVALID CASE rather than only asserted - a direct base-to-apex transfer, neither axis centroidal, with the axes 60 mm apart, would give 1620000 + 2700(3600) = 11340000 mm^4 against the correct 4860000, an overshoot of a factor of 2.33, and procedure step 5 authors the rejection and replacement of that route as its own step rather than leaving it to a caution; and BOTH transfer directions are exercised, one subtracting toward the centroid and one adding away from it. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution, in two parts: first, checking the theorem against itself is CIRCULAR, since transferring out and back returns the starting value regardless of whether the reference axis was chosen correctly; second, the POSITIVITY check that a transferred value must exceed the centroidal one catches a DIRECTION error - subtracting while moving away gives 540000 - 1080000 = -540000, negative and therefore caught - but is BLIND to a WRONG REFERENCE, because the invalid direct transfer returns 11340000, comfortably positive and still wrong. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays, and it is the strongest in this batch because it is genuinely independent rather than self-referential: transfer 1 reproduces the centroidal value that a DIFFERENT signed skill obtained by a DIFFERENT method, so the agreement tests the theorem rather than restating it. That independence exists only because area_moment_integral_definition deliberately DECLINED to connect its base result to the centroidal standard value and ceded the connection here, which is what made the two endpoints independent evidence. THREE-signal mapping with chained triggers: axis_confusion at step 2 (identifying WHICH axis is the centroidal reference that anchors the relation; treating a non-centroidal axis as that anchor is a misidentification of the axis the theorem is built around, the same class of earn as identifying a longitudinal versus a transverse axis in torque_internal_loading; its trigger opens by stipulating the shape and named parallel axes have been identified), sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (adding when moving toward the centroidal axis, subtracting when moving away, or using a distance that is not the perpendicular separation; its trigger opens by stipulating the centroidal reference has been identified, which partitions it from step 2), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - re-deriving a centroidal value instead of taking it as given, integrating, combining multiple shapes, applying a direct transfer without routing through the centroid, skipping verification, or reporting without a named axis and length^4 units). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED with explicit argument: the invalid direct base-to-apex transfer is a WRONG-REFERENCE error, not an out-of-order solve. The theorem simply does not hold between two non-centroidal axes and nothing is left underivable at that point; the corpus standard is that sequencing requires an unknown to be STRANDED, as at a truss joint carrying three unknowns against two equations in method_of_joints, and the fact that the correct route happens to take two steps does not by itself earn the signal. This holds the same line drawn at method_of_sections, where over-cutting was routed away from sequencing as a cut-selection error. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent; its scope question arises at position 4 of this batch, where composite summation begins. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Unlocks composite_area_moment_of_inertia.

ordered_steps: Identify the given section area A and each given area moment of inertia I about a named axis. Take I and A as given; do not re-derive them, do not integrate, and do not transfer axes. Do not treat k as transferable by the parallel-axis relation.

For each required result, fix the named axis and select the I that belongs to that same axis. Do not pair an I from one axis with a k labelled for another, and do not treat k as a single axis-independent property of the section.
Form the ratio I / A for that axis. Units of the ratio are length^2.
Take the positive square root to obtain k = sqrt(I / A). Confirm that k has length units; a result with length^2 units means the square root was omitted.
If more than one named axis is required, repeat the axis pairing and extraction for each axis so that each k is labelled for its own axis.

Verify before reporting by the inverse form on a different route from the division: compute A k^2 for each axis and confirm that it recovers the given I for that axis. Record that this check confirms the arithmetic of the extraction only and does not validate the given I or A.
Report each k with its named axis and length units. Stop. Do not re-derive I, integrate, transfer k, or extend into mass radius of gyration or other-subject applications.

signature.notes: Radius of gyration of an area about a stated axis, k = sqrt(I / A), with I and A taken as given and not re-derived. Independently re-derived: I_x / A = 12000000 / 7500 = 1600 mm^2, k_x = 40 mm; I_y / A = 3000000 / 7500 = 400 mm^2, k_y = 20 mm. Verified by the inverse form on a different route: A k_x^2 = 7500(1600) = 12000000 mm^4 recovering I_x, and A k_y^2 = 7500(400) = 3000000 mm^4 recovering I_y. The two k values differ by a factor of two for the same section, establishing that k is per-axis and not a single property of the section. Boundary recorded: k does NOT transfer by the parallel-axis relation — a k about another axis requires transferring I first and recomputing; no integration; mass radius of gyration excluded as a deferred node. CROSS_SUBJECT_BRIDGE handled as one concept sentence with no buckling formulae, effective length, or slenderness limits; that application belongs to MECHANICS_OF_MATERIALS. Two earned signals: axis_confusion at step 2, unclassified at step 7. sign_or_placement_error and solution_sequencing_error omitted as unearned, not trimmed — omitting the square root or inverting the ratio is an operational error rather than sign or placement, and both I and A are given so no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used unearned: no averaging step is authored. Honest limitation recorded in the artifact: the back-substitution confirms extraction arithmetic only and cannot validate the given I or A. OPERATOR NOTE, non-blocking, logged for Architect review: the unclassified trigger absorbs the missing-square-root and inverted-ratio errors but targets step 7, while those errors are authored at step 4. Escalation for this skill's characteristic error therefore lands on the reporting step rather than the failing step. Accepted here under corpus precedent for terminal-step unclassified mapping; flagged as a candidate for enum or mapping review.

ordered_steps: Decompose the composite section into simple shapes. Take the composite centroid location as given from composite_centroid; do not re-derive it. Take each shape's area A_i and own centroidal value I_i as given from area_moment_of_inertia; do not re-derive those values and do not integrate. Cite that parallel_axis_theorem_area supplies the per-shape transfer relation used below.

Identify the common axis for the assembly — typically the composite centroidal axis — and, for each shape, that shape's own centroid. Measure each transfer distance d_i from that shape's centroid to the common axis. Do not use one distance for all shapes, and do not measure from an unrelated reference such as the base when the common axis is the composite centroid.
For each shape, form the transfer term A_i d_i^2 using that shape's own A_i and d_i.
Form each shape's contribution as I_i + A_i d_i^2. Do not omit the transfer term; summing the constituent centroidal values alone is not a valid assembly about the common axis.
Sum the contributions: I_total = Σ (I_i + A_i d_i^2). Units are length^4.

Verify before reporting by reaching the same total on a different route when practical: assemble about another parallel axis (for example the base) using each shape's own distance to that axis, then transfer the whole section as a single body of area A from that axis to the composite centroid using the parallel-axis relation. Agreement confirms the assembly and the transfer distances; it does not validate the constituent I_i inputs.
Report I_total with the named common axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not re-derive the composite centroid, re-derive constituent standard results, integrate, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Composite assembly about a common axis from per-shape centroidal values plus per-shape transfer terms. Independently re-derived: d_flange = 24 mm and d_web = 36 mm, each measured from that shape's own centroid to the composite centroidal axis at y_bar = 81 mm; contributions 3515400 and 7095600; I_total = 10611000 mm^4. Verified by the independent base route: I_base = 69660000 mm^4, then whole-section transfer 69660000 - 9000(81)^2 = 10611000 mm^4, agreeing exactly. Composite centroid taken as given from composite_centroid and cross-checked consistent at 81 mm; not re-derived in the artifact. Complement to parallel_axis_theorem_area recorded: this skill applies the transfer relation once per shape and sums, and does not re-derive the relation. simple_average_used is unearned here because the composite centroid is given and no averaging step is authored; this is a scoping consequence, and the general question of whether the Centroids-family restriction reaches the MOI family remains OPEN with the Architect and is NOT answered by this sign-off. solution_sequencing_error omitted: the given centroid strands no prerequisite unknown. Three earned signals at steps 2, 4, 7. Honest limitation recorded in the artifact: the consistency check validates the composition, not the constituent inputs.

ordered_steps: Name the stated pair of perpendicular axes about which I_xy is required. The product of inertia is defined only with respect to that stated pair; do not mix a coordinate measured from one reference with a coordinate measured from another. Cite that area_moment_integral_definition owns the integral definition of the second moment of area; this skill uses the same integral machinery with integrand x y: I_xy = ∫ x y dA. Do not re-derive the definitional apparatus. Do not introduce mass, density, an angle of rotation, or Mohr's circle.

Decompose the area into simple shapes. Cite the composite assembly logic from composite_area_moment_of_inertia; do not re-derive it. For each shape, record A_i and the centroid coordinates (x_i, y_i) relative to the stated axes, retaining signs.

For each shape, obtain I_xy_c about its own centroidal axes parallel to the stated pair. For a rectangle with sides parallel to the axes, I_xy_c = 0 because each of those centroidal axes is an axis of symmetry of the rectangle. State the either-axis condition: I_xy vanishes whenever either of the two axes is an axis of symmetry of the area — not both, either.

Apply the product parallel-axis relation for each shape: I_xy = I_xy_c + A x_bar y_bar, using that shape's A, x_bar, and y_bar (or A_i, x_i, y_i). Contrast with parallel_axis_theorem_area: the transfer term for I_x or I_y is A d^2 and is always non-negative; the product transfer term is A x_bar y_bar and may be negative. Do not re-derive the parallel-axis theorem.

Form each shape's contribution as I_xy_c,i + A_i x_i y_i, retaining the sign of the product x_i y_i. Sum the contributions: I_xy = Σ (I_xy_c,i + A_i x_i y_i). Do not treat the transfer term as necessarily positive by analogy with A d^2.

Interpret the sign and the zero case. A negative I_xy is allowed and has no counterpart in I_x or I_y, which integrate squares and are always positive for a real area. A zero I_xy records that the area is symmetrically disposed about at least one of the two axes; it does not mean the area is absent.

Verify before reporting by reaching the same total on a genuinely different decomposition when practical (for example a negative-area route). Agreement confirms that the decomposition and the transfer arithmetic were done consistently; it does not validate the axes themselves.

Report I_xy with the named axis pair and length^4 units. Stop. Do not rotate axes, introduce an angle, construct Mohr's circle, introduce mass or density, re-derive the parallel-axis theorem, or treat a zero result as an absent area.

signature.notes: Product of inertia of an area about a stated pair of perpendicular axes, opening Batch 4M and unlocking inclined_axis_area_moment. Independently re-derived. Case 1, an L-shape decomposed into two rectangles: R1 contributes 1600(40)(10) = 640000 mm^4 and R2 contributes 1200(10)(50) = 600000 mm^4, giving I_xy = 1240000 mm^4, with each rectangle's own centroidal product zero because its sides are parallel to the axes and each centroidal axis is therefore a symmetry axis. Verified by a genuinely different decomposition rather than a restatement: the same L equals an 80 by 80 square less a 60 by 60 square, giving 6400(40)(40) - 3600(50)(50) = 10240000 - 9000000 = 1240000 mm^4, agreeing exactly. Read the principal moments as the circle extrema: I_max = I_avg + R and I_min = I_avg − R. These are where the circle crosses the horizontal axis. Do not treat the reference x-y pair as already principal when I_xy is nonzero.

Determine the principal orientation under the project's signed convention: solve tan 2theta_p = −I_xy / ((I_x − I_y)/2) and select the branch that makes signed I_uv vanish. ordered_steps: State the complement in one sentence: product_of_inertia_area COMPUTES the product of inertia; this skill INTERPRETS its sign, its symmetry-driven vanishing, and its axis-dependence. Declare the symbols I_xy (signed, length^4), I_x and I_y (always positive for contrast), and element coordinates x and y. Name the exclusions: do not compute a numeric I_xy, do not assemble a composite by summing A_i x_i y_i, do not apply the parallel-axis transfer, do not construct Mohr's circle or compute a principal angle (owned by mohrs_circle_area_moment), do not re-derive the inclined-axis transformation (owned by inclined_axis_area_moment), and do not introduce mass or dynamics. Cite area_moment_of_inertia only for the contrast that I_x and I_y are always positive.

Interpret the SIGN of I_xy from quadrant placement. For each described region, determine whether x and y share a sign (first/third quadrants → integrand x y positive) or differ (second/fourth → integrand x y negative). Conclude I_xy > 0 or I_xy < 0 from that sign reasoning alone. Do not evaluate a numeric magnitude.

Apply the SYMMETRY ZERO CONDITION. Identify whether either the x-axis or the y-axis is an axis of symmetry of the area. If so, argue that each element pairs with a mirror element whose x y contribution is equal and opposite, so the contributions cancel and I_xy = 0. Name which axis is the symmetry axis used in the argument. State that either axis alone suffices. Do not compute the integral to reach zero.

Reason about AXIS DEPENDENCE. State that I_xy depends on the orientation of the axis pair. For a general area with nonzero I_xy about a reference pair, argue that as the axes rotate I_xy varies continuously and, because it can be positive at some orientations and negative at others, there must exist an orientation at which I_xy = 0 — the principal orientation. Name that orientation in words. Do not compute the angle and do not construct Mohr's circle.

State the interpretive consequence: because I_xy may be positive, negative, or zero while I_x and I_y are always positive, I_xy is the quantity that couples the two axes, and its vanishing is what defines the principal directions. Record the false converse: I_xy = 0 does not imply a symmetry axis, because a principal orientation of an asymmetric area also gives zero.

Verify before reporting by a consistency check of the three interpretive conclusions against each other, with no computation. Confirm that Cases 1–3 are mutually consistent under one principle — that I_xy is a signed, axis-dependent measure that symmetry can force to zero: Case 1 shows a nonzero signed value under asymmetric placement, Case 2 shows zero under symmetry, and Case 3 shows a rotation that reaches zero. Confirm none contradicts another: an area with a symmetry axis (Case 2) is already at a principal orientation (Case 3 with the vanishing orientation being the symmetry axis itself). Record the honest limitation: interpretation fixes sign and vanishing conditions, not magnitude; zero does not prove symmetry.

Report the three interpretive conclusions — sign from quadrant reasoning, zero from the named symmetry axis, and existence of a principal orientation where I_xy vanishes — without any computed I_xy value, composite assembly, parallel-axis transfer, Mohr construction, or principal angle. Stop.

For each named centroidal axis, identify which dimension is perpendicular to that axis — that dimension is raised to the third power. Do not interchange the parallel and perpendicular dimensions.
Select the established standard result for the shape and axis: rectangle I_x = b h^3 / 12 and I_y = h b^3 / 12; triangle I = b h^3 / 36 about the centroidal axis parallel to the base.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 1/5, batch open, and the FIRST signed procedure in STATICS_MOMENTS_OF_INERTIA - a topic that held zero signed procedures before this commit. Owns computation of the AREA MOMENT OF INERTIA, the second moment of area, for SIMPLE SHAPES about their own CENTROIDAL axes using established standard results: what the quantity measures (resistance to bending about a named axis), its units of length to the fourth power, the fact that I is always taken about a NAMED axis so the same shape generally has different values about different axes, and the rule that the dimension PERPENDICULAR to the named axis is the one raised to the third power. Boundary: centroid_first_moments (signed prerequisite) computes FIRST moments of area, integrals of the form y dA, used to locate a centroid, while this skill computes the SECOND moment, integrals of the form y squared dA; the artifact states plainly that these are different quantities with different units, which is the distinction most at risk of collapsing between adjacent Centroids and Moments-of-Inertia content. area_moment_integral_definition (batch sibling, position 2, not yet signed) owns the integral definition and its evaluation by integration; this skill APPLIES established standard results and does not derive them, naming the sibling as owner - a forward cession of the kind used in Batches 4I and 4J. parallel_axis_theorem_area (position 3) owns transfer to a non-centroidal axis, so this skill is restricted to centroidal axes only. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (position 4) and radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) are excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived and independently recomputed: a rectangle of width b = 40 mm along x and height h = 60 mm along y, about centroidal axes, gives I_x = b h^3 / 12 = 40 (216000) / 12 = 720000 mm^4 and I_y = h b^3 / 12 = 60 (64000) / 12 = 320000 mm^4; a triangle of base b = 90 mm and height h = 60 mm about the centroidal axis parallel to its base gives I = b h^3 / 36 = 90 (216000) / 36 = 540000 mm^4. Distinguishing feature bites: the section is NON-SQUARE and BOTH centroidal axes are computed, so the two values differ and the choice of axis is decisive - a square section would make an interchanged calculation undetectable; and a SECOND shape carrying a DIFFERENT standard denominator, 36 rather than 12, prevents a student from applying one formula universally. The four candidate errors produce four distinct values: correct 720000, dimensions interchanged 320000, triangle formula applied to the rectangle 240000, and squared instead of cubed 12000. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution, and it is why the example is 40 by 60 rather than square: the DIMENSIONAL check that I must come out in length to the fourth power catches an exponent error such as squaring instead of cubing, but is BLIND to interchanging the two dimensions because both orderings give the same units; the MAGNITUDE check, that the larger perpendicular dimension must give the larger I and that I_x / I_y must equal (h/b) squared, DOES catch an interchange, but only because the section is non-square - for a square section the two values would be equal and neither check would detect it. The two checks are deliberately asymmetric and the artifact states what each catches and what it misses. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays. TWO-signal mapping: axis_confusion at step 2 (CENTRAL - identifying which dimension is perpendicular to the named axis and therefore cubed; its trigger opens by stipulating that the shape and named centroidal axes have been identified, which partitions it from the standard-result selection that follows), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - wrong standard result for the shape, derivation by integration instead of the established result, a centroidal result applied to a non-centroidal axis, skipped verification, or reporting without the named axis and length^4 units). sign_or_placement_error OMITTED with explicit argument: an area moment of inertia about a centroidal axis is always positive and no authored step assigns a sign, so nothing earns it. solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the three computations are independent and no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent: the canonical restriction confines it to the Centroids family, and whether that restriction extends to composite moments of inertia is an open question that will arise at position 4 of this batch, not here; it was not reached for. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Operator observation recorded, not corrected: common_errors carries seven entries against the five typical of signed artifacts, and three of them - squaring instead of cubing, omitting units or the named axis, and computing only one centroidal axis when both are required - all route to the single unclassified mapping at step 7. This is finer-grained error enumeration than the two mapped signals can discriminate, a milder instance of the pattern recorded at seven-to-one on zero_force_members in Batch 4J, and it is carried to the pending signal-taxonomy ruling rather than corrected here. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Opens Batch 4K; unlocks area_moment_integral_definition and radius_of_gyration_area.

ordered_steps: Identify the shape, dimensions, and named axis. State that this skill derives I by integration and does not take a standard closed form as given — complement to area_moment_of_inertia. Cite that centroid_first_moments uses ∫ y dA while this skill uses ∫ y^2 dA. Do not use a parallel-axis transfer.

Construct the differential area element so that the squared coordinate in the integrand is constant over the element. For I_x or I_base the integrand is y^2, so use a horizontal strip of thickness dy; a vertical strip would leave y varying over the element and invalidate a single integral in y.

Express dA for that strip. If the shape is not a rectangle, write the strip width as a function of the integration variable (for a triangle with base b at y = 0 and apex at y = h, width = b(1 - y/h)).

Set the integration limits that place the named axis. Centroidal limits for a rectangle of height h about its centroidal x-axis run from y = -h/2 to y = +h/2; limits about a base run from y = 0 to y = h. Changing the limits changes which axis the result is about.
Evaluate the integral: form the antiderivative, substitute the limits, and simplify to a closed form. Then substitute any given numeric dimensions. Units are length^4.

Verify before reporting. Where a standard result for the same shape and the same axis is already known from area_moment_of_inertia, cross-check the derived closed form and numeric value against it. Where no such same-axis standard exists, check dimensions (length^4) and re-check the element construction and limits; do not connect to a different-axis tabulated value by a transfer relation.

Report each derived I with the named axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not quote an underived standard result as the answer, transfer to a parallel axis, combine shapes, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 2/5. Owns the INTEGRAL DEFINITION of the area moment of inertia and its EVALUATION: the definitions I_x = integral of y squared dA and I_y = integral of x squared dA; constructing the differential area element so the SQUARED COORDINATE IS CONSTANT OVER THE ELEMENT, which is why the integrand in y squared forces a horizontal strip; expressing a varying element width as a function of the integration variable when the shape is not a rectangle; setting integration limits that determine WHICH axis the result is about; and evaluating to a closed form. The artifact ACTUALLY INTEGRATES rather than quoting - both closed forms emerge from evaluated integrals with the antiderivative formed and the limits substituted, and standard results are the OUTPUT of this procedure rather than an input to it, which was the single largest risk on this skill. Boundary: area_moment_of_inertia (signed, skill 1 of this batch) APPLIES established standard results for simple shapes about centroidal axes and explicitly cedes derivation here; the artifact carries the complement - this skill derives those results and does not take them as given. centroid_first_moments (signed) computes FIRST moments, the integral of y dA, while this skill computes the SECOND moment, the integral of y squared dA; the artifact states that the integrand differs by one power of the coordinate. parallel_axis_theorem_area (batch sibling, position 3, not yet signed) owns the TRANSFER relation between a centroidal axis and a parallel one; this skill obtains a value about whichever axis its integration LIMITS select, by direct integration only, and names position 3 as owner of the connection rather than performing it - a forward cession. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (position 4) and radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived symbolically and numerically. Case 1, rectangle of width b and height h about the CENTROIDAL x axis: horizontal strip of width b and thickness dy so dA = b dy with every point at the same y, limits from -h/2 to +h/2 because the axis passes through the centroid; I_x = b times the antiderivative y cubed over 3 evaluated between those limits = b(h cubed over 24 plus h cubed over 24) = b h cubed over 12; with b = 40 mm and h = 60 mm, I_x = 720000 mm^4. Case 2, triangle of base b along the x axis with apex at height h, about the BASE: the width is not constant, narrowing linearly from b at y = 0 to zero at y = h so the width is b(1 - y/h) and dA = b(1 - y/h) dy, limits from 0 to h; I_base = b times the integral of y squared minus y cubed over h = b times the antiderivative y cubed over 3 minus y to the fourth over 4h evaluated at h = b(h cubed over 3 minus h cubed over 4) = b h cubed over 12; with b = 90 mm and h = 60 mm, I_base = 1620000 mm^4. The artifact notes that the same closed form b h cubed over 12 arises for both cases even though shape and axis both differ, and states explicitly that the coincidence of form is not a shortcut. Distinguishing feature bites: the element construction is DECISIVE and the artifact states why the strip orientation follows from the integrand rather than asserting it; a SECOND shape whose element WIDTH VARIES with the integration variable appears, so the method cannot reduce to pulling a constant out of the integral; and the integration LIMITS are shown to determine which axis the result is about, with the rectangle taken from 0 to h instead of -h/2 to +h/2 returning 2880000 rather than 720000. Three candidate errors give three distinct values for case 1 - correct 720000, wrong limits 2880000, integrating x squared instead of y squared 320000 - and a constant-width element applied to the triangle gives 6480000 against the correct 1620000. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution: checking a derived result against a tabulated standard value is available ONLY where such a value already exists FOR THAT AXIS. Case 1 cross-checks against the rectangle-about-centroidal-x result applied by area_moment_of_inertia and agrees at 720000. Case 2 has NO same-axis cross-check, because area_moment_of_inertia supplied the triangle's CENTROIDAL value of 540000 mm^4, a different axis from the base; connecting them requires the transfer relation owned by parallel_axis_theorem_area and is deliberately not performed, so for case 2 the available checks are dimensional and the element construction itself. Where no tabulated same-axis value exists the integration must stand on its own element construction and limits, which is why those steps carry the weight rather than the arithmetic. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays. THREE-signal mapping with chained triggers: axis_confusion at step 2 (constructing the element so the squared coordinate is constant over it, and integrating the correct coordinate for the named axis; its trigger opens by stipulating the shape and named axis have been identified), sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (the integration LIMITS place the axis; its trigger opens by stipulating a correctly oriented strip, which partitions it from step 2), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - quoting a standard closed form instead of deriving it, using a transfer relation, applying a constant-width element to the triangle, skipping verification, or reporting without a named axis and length^4 units). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the two cases are independent and no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent; its scope question arises at position 4 of this batch. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. OPERATOR OBSERVATION RECORDED AND ROUTED TO THE PENDING TAXONOMY RULING, not corrected: procedure step 3, which expresses a varying element width as a function of the integration variable, carries no dedicated signal, so the error of pulling a constant width out of the integral routes to unclassified at step 7 alongside five other classes. Splitting element ORIENTATION at step 2, which is genuinely an axis error, from element WIDTH EXPRESSION at step 3, which is not, was the honest choice, and none of the canonical five names the act of pulling a varying factor out of an integral. This is notable beyond the general vocabulary gap already recorded three times, because here it is the skill's own DISTINGUISHING FEATURE whose error mode is undiagnosable - the varying-width shape is required precisely so the method cannot reduce to a constant, and a student who makes exactly that reduction cannot be routed to a remedy. No new signal is proposed and none was force-fit. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Unlocks parallel_axis_theorem_area.

ordered_steps: Identify the single shape, its area A, the named parallel axes, and any I values taken as given. Cite that area_moment_of_inertia supplies centroidal standard results without transferring, and area_moment_integral_definition obtains an axis value by integration without transferring. Do not re-derive those given values and do not integrate. Do not sum multiple shapes.
Identify which of the named axes is the centroidal reference that must anchor I = I_c + A d^2. Do not treat a non-centroidal axis as the reference of the relation.
For each required transfer, determine the perpendicular distance d between the two parallel axes involved and form A d^2.

Apply the theorem in the correct direction: add A d^2 when moving away from the centroidal axis; subtract A d^2 when moving toward it. If neither endpoint is the centroidal axis, transfer through the centroidal axis in two steps. Do not apply the relation directly between two non-centroidal axes.
If a direct transfer between two non-centroidal axes is proposed, reject it and replace it with the two-step route through the centroidal axis.

Verify before reporting. Prefer agreement with an independently obtained value for the same axis when available. Check positivity: transferred values about non-centroidal axes must exceed I_c. Record that positivity catches a direction error but does not catch a wrong-reference direct transfer, and that transferring out and back is circular as a check of the reference choice.
Report each transferred I with the named axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not integrate, re-derive centroidal standard results, combine shapes, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Batch 4K skill 3/5. Owns the TRANSFER of an area moment of inertia between PARALLEL axes: the relation I = I_c + A d squared with I_c about the CENTROIDAL axis, A the area and d the PERPENDICULAR distance between the two parallel axes; the requirement that the reference axis in the relation is ALWAYS the centroidal one; the direction of transfer, adding when moving away from the centroidal axis and subtracting when moving toward it; and the consequence that because A d squared cannot be negative the centroidal axis gives the MINIMUM value among all parallel axes. Boundary: area_moment_of_inertia (signed, skill 1) supplies centroidal values from established standard results and restricted itself to centroidal axes, ceding transfer here; the artifact carries the complement - this skill transfers and does not re-derive centroidal values. area_moment_integral_definition (signed, skill 2) obtains a value about whichever axis its integration limits select, by direct integration only, and explicitly named this skill as owner of the connection between parallel axes; the artifact carries that complement too - this skill connects by the theorem and does not integrate. composite_area_moment_of_inertia (batch sibling, position 4, not yet signed) combines several shapes each generally requiring its own transfer; this skill transfers ONE shape and does not sum contributions - a forward cession. radius_of_gyration_area (position 5) excluded. Worked example Operator-re-derived and independently recomputed: triangle of base b = 90 mm and height h = 60 mm, area A = 2700 mm squared, centroid h/3 = 20 mm above the base. Two endpoint values are taken as GIVEN and not re-derived, and critically they were obtained by DIFFERENT METHODS in two already-signed artifacts - I_c = 540000 mm^4 about the centroidal axis, from area_moment_of_inertia applying the standard result b h cubed over 36, and I_base = 1620000 mm^4 about the base, from area_moment_integral_definition evaluating the integral directly. Transfer 1, base to centroidal, moving TOWARD the centroid so SUBTRACT: d = 20 mm, A d squared = 2700(400) = 1080000, giving I_c = 1620000 - 1080000 = 540000 mm^4. Transfer 2, centroidal to an axis through the apex, moving AWAY so ADD: the apex is 60 mm above the base and the centroid 20 mm above it so d = 40 mm, A d squared = 2700(1600) = 4320000, giving I_apex = 540000 + 4320000 = 4860000 mm^4. The Operator independently confirmed I_apex against direct integration, which gives b h cubed over 4 = 4860000 mm^4 for these dimensions. Distinguishing feature bites: the CENTROIDAL REFERENCE requirement is contradicted by a WORKED INVALID CASE rather than only asserted - a direct base-to-apex transfer, neither axis centroidal, with the axes 60 mm apart, would give 1620000 + 2700(3600) = 11340000 mm^4 against the correct 4860000, an overshoot of a factor of 2.33, and procedure step 5 authors the rejection and replacement of that route as its own step rather than leaving it to a caution; and BOTH transfer directions are exercised, one subtracting toward the centroid and one adding away from it. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure and solution, in two parts: first, checking the theorem against itself is CIRCULAR, since transferring out and back returns the starting value regardless of whether the reference axis was chosen correctly; second, the POSITIVITY check that a transferred value must exceed the centroidal one catches a DIRECTION error - subtracting while moving away gives 540000 - 1080000 = -540000, negative and therefore caught - but is BLIND to a WRONG REFERENCE, because the invalid direct transfer returns 11340000, comfortably positive and still wrong. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays, and it is the strongest in this batch because it is genuinely independent rather than self-referential: transfer 1 reproduces the centroidal value that a DIFFERENT signed skill obtained by a DIFFERENT method, so the agreement tests the theorem rather than restating it. That independence exists only because area_moment_integral_definition deliberately DECLINED to connect its base result to the centroidal standard value and ceded the connection here, which is what made the two endpoints independent evidence. THREE-signal mapping with chained triggers: axis_confusion at step 2 (identifying WHICH axis is the centroidal reference that anchors the relation; treating a non-centroidal axis as that anchor is a misidentification of the axis the theorem is built around, the same class of earn as identifying a longitudinal versus a transverse axis in torque_internal_loading; its trigger opens by stipulating the shape and named parallel axes have been identified), sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (adding when moving toward the centroidal axis, subtracting when moving away, or using a distance that is not the perpendicular separation; its trigger opens by stipulating the centroidal reference has been identified, which partitions it from step 2), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - re-deriving a centroidal value instead of taking it as given, integrating, combining multiple shapes, applying a direct transfer without routing through the centroid, skipping verification, or reporting without a named axis and length^4 units). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED with explicit argument: the invalid direct base-to-apex transfer is a WRONG-REFERENCE error, not an out-of-order solve. The theorem simply does not hold between two non-centroidal axes and nothing is left underivable at that point; the corpus standard is that sequencing requires an unknown to be STRANDED, as at a truss joint carrying three unknowns against two equations in method_of_joints, and the fact that the correct route happens to take two steps does not by itself earn the signal. This holds the same line drawn at method_of_sections, where over-cutting was routed away from sequencing as a cut-selection error. simple_average_used FORBIDDEN and absent; its scope question arises at position 4 of this batch, where composite summation begins. Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane. Unlocks composite_area_moment_of_inertia.

ordered_steps: Identify the given section area A and each given area moment of inertia I about a named axis. Take I and A as given; do not re-derive them, do not integrate, and do not transfer axes. Do not treat k as transferable by the parallel-axis relation.

For each required result, fix the named axis and select the I that belongs to that same axis. Do not pair an I from one axis with a k labelled for another, and do not treat k as a single axis-independent property of the section.
Form the ratio I / A for that axis. Units of the ratio are length^2.
Take the positive square root to obtain k = sqrt(I / A). Confirm that k has length units; a result with length^2 units means the square root was omitted.
If more than one named axis is required, repeat the axis pairing and extraction for each axis so that each k is labelled for its own axis.

Verify before reporting by the inverse form on a different route from the division: compute A k^2 for each axis and confirm that it recovers the given I for that axis. Record that this check confirms the arithmetic of the extraction only and does not validate the given I or A.
Report each k with its named axis and length units. Stop. Do not re-derive I, integrate, transfer k, or extend into mass radius of gyration or other-subject applications.

signature.notes: Radius of gyration of an area about a stated axis, k = sqrt(I / A), with I and A taken as given and not re-derived. Independently re-derived: I_x / A = 12000000 / 7500 = 1600 mm^2, k_x = 40 mm; I_y / A = 3000000 / 7500 = 400 mm^2, k_y = 20 mm. Verified by the inverse form on a different route: A k_x^2 = 7500(1600) = 12000000 mm^4 recovering I_x, and A k_y^2 = 7500(400) = 3000000 mm^4 recovering I_y. The two k values differ by a factor of two for the same section, establishing that k is per-axis and not a single property of the section. Boundary recorded: k does NOT transfer by the parallel-axis relation — a k about another axis requires transferring I first and recomputing; no integration; mass radius of gyration excluded as a deferred node. CROSS_SUBJECT_BRIDGE handled as one concept sentence with no buckling formulae, effective length, or slenderness limits; that application belongs to MECHANICS_OF_MATERIALS. Two earned signals: axis_confusion at step 2, unclassified at step 7. sign_or_placement_error and solution_sequencing_error omitted as unearned, not trimmed — omitting the square root or inverting the ratio is an operational error rather than sign or placement, and both I and A are given so no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used unearned: no averaging step is authored. Honest limitation recorded in the artifact: the back-substitution confirms extraction arithmetic only and cannot validate the given I or A. OPERATOR NOTE, non-blocking, logged for Architect review: the unclassified trigger absorbs the missing-square-root and inverted-ratio errors but targets step 7, while those errors are authored at step 4. Escalation for this skill's characteristic error therefore lands on the reporting step rather than the failing step. Accepted here under corpus precedent for terminal-step unclassified mapping; flagged as a candidate for enum or mapping review.

ordered_steps: Decompose the composite section into simple shapes. Take the composite centroid location as given from composite_centroid; do not re-derive it. Take each shape's area A_i and own centroidal value I_i as given from area_moment_of_inertia; do not re-derive those values and do not integrate. Cite that parallel_axis_theorem_area supplies the per-shape transfer relation used below.

Identify the common axis for the assembly — typically the composite centroidal axis — and, for each shape, that shape's own centroid. Measure each transfer distance d_i from that shape's centroid to the common axis. Do not use one distance for all shapes, and do not measure from an unrelated reference such as the base when the common axis is the composite centroid.
For each shape, form the transfer term A_i d_i^2 using that shape's own A_i and d_i.
Form each shape's contribution as I_i + A_i d_i^2. Do not omit the transfer term; summing the constituent centroidal values alone is not a valid assembly about the common axis.
Sum the contributions: I_total = Σ (I_i + A_i d_i^2). Units are length^4.

Verify before reporting by reaching the same total on a different route when practical: assemble about another parallel axis (for example the base) using each shape's own distance to that axis, then transfer the whole section as a single body of area A from that axis to the composite centroid using the parallel-axis relation. Agreement confirms the assembly and the transfer distances; it does not validate the constituent I_i inputs.
Report I_total with the named common axis and length^4 units. Stop. Do not re-derive the composite centroid, re-derive constituent standard results, integrate, or compute radius of gyration.

signature.notes: Composite assembly about a common axis from per-shape centroidal values plus per-shape transfer terms. Independently re-derived: d_flange = 24 mm and d_web = 36 mm, each measured from that shape's own centroid to the composite centroidal axis at y_bar = 81 mm; contributions 3515400 and 7095600; I_total = 10611000 mm^4. Verified by the independent base route: I_base = 69660000 mm^4, then whole-section transfer 69660000 - 9000(81)^2 = 10611000 mm^4, agreeing exactly. Composite centroid taken as given from composite_centroid and cross-checked consistent at 81 mm; not re-derived in the artifact. Complement to parallel_axis_theorem_area recorded: this skill applies the transfer relation once per shape and sums, and does not re-derive the relation. simple_average_used is unearned here because the composite centroid is given and no averaging step is authored; this is a scoping consequence, and the general question of whether the Centroids-family restriction reaches the MOI family remains OPEN with the Architect and is NOT answered by this sign-off. solution_sequencing_error omitted: the given centroid strands no prerequisite unknown. Three earned signals at steps 2, 4, 7. Honest limitation recorded in the artifact: the consistency check validates the composition, not the constituent inputs.

ordered_steps: Name the stated pair of perpendicular axes about which I_xy is required. The product of inertia is defined only with respect to that stated pair; do not mix a coordinate measured from one reference with a coordinate measured from another. Cite that area_moment_integral_definition owns the integral definition of the second moment of area; this skill uses the same integral machinery with integrand x y: I_xy = ∫ x y dA. Do not re-derive the definitional apparatus. Do not introduce mass, density, an angle of rotation, or Mohr's circle.

Decompose the area into simple shapes. Cite the composite assembly logic from composite_area_moment_of_inertia; do not re-derive it. For each shape, record A_i and the centroid coordinates (x_i, y_i) relative to the stated axes, retaining signs.

For each shape, obtain I_xy_c about its own centroidal axes parallel to the stated pair. For a rectangle with sides parallel to the axes, I_xy_c = 0 because each of those centroidal axes is an axis of symmetry of the rectangle. State the either-axis condition: I_xy vanishes whenever either of the two axes is an axis of symmetry of the area — not both, either.

Apply the product parallel-axis relation for each shape: I_xy = I_xy_c + A x_bar y_bar, using that shape's A, x_bar, and y_bar (or A_i, x_i, y_i). Contrast with parallel_axis_theorem_area: the transfer term for I_x or I_y is A d^2 and is always non-negative; the product transfer term is A x_bar y_bar and may be negative. Do not re-derive the parallel-axis theorem.

Form each shape's contribution as I_xy_c,i + A_i x_i y_i, retaining the sign of the product x_i y_i. Sum the contributions: I_xy = Σ (I_xy_c,i + A_i x_i y_i). Do not treat the transfer term as necessarily positive by analogy with A d^2.

Interpret the sign and the zero case. A negative I_xy is allowed and has no counterpart in I_x or I_y, which integrate squares and are always positive for a real area. A zero I_xy records that the area is symmetrically disposed about at least one of the two axes; it does not mean the area is absent.

Verify before reporting by reaching the same total on a genuinely different decomposition when practical (for example a negative-area route). Agreement confirms that the decomposition and the transfer arithmetic were done consistently; it does not validate the axes themselves.

Report I_xy with the named axis pair and length^4 units. Stop. Do not rotate axes, introduce an angle, construct Mohr's circle, introduce mass or density, re-derive the parallel-axis theorem, or treat a zero result as an absent area.

signature.notes: Product of inertia of an area about a stated pair of perpendicular axes, opening Batch 4M and unlocking inclined_axis_area_moment. Independently re-derived. Case 1, an L-shape decomposed into two rectangles: R1 contributes 1600(40)(10) = 640000 mm^4 and R2 contributes 1200(10)(50) = 600000 mm^4, giving I_xy = 1240000 mm^4, with each rectangle's own centroidal product zero because its sides are parallel to the axes and each centroidal axis is therefore a symmetry axis. Verified by a genuinely different decomposition rather than a restatement: the same L equals an 80 by 80 square less a 60 by 60 square, giving 6400(40)(40) - 3600(50)(50) = 10240000 - 9000000 = 1240000 mm^4, agreeing exactly. All three distinguishing behaviours of the product of inertia are exercised rather than asserted. NEGATIVITY: Case 3 reflects R1 into the second quadrant, giving 1600(-40)(10) = -640000 mm^4, equal in magnitude to R1's positive contribution and opposite in sign, with the artifact recording that this has no counterpart in I_x or I_y, which integrate squares and are always positive for a real area. ZERO BY SYMMETRY: Case 2 uses a rectangle centred on the origin, giving I_xy = 0 with area 3200 mm^2 plainly present, and the artifact states both that a zero records symmetric disposition rather than absent area and that only ONE of the two axes need be a symmetry axis — the either-axis condition, not both. SIGNED TRANSFER: the product parallel-axis relation I_xy = I_xy_c + A x_bar y_bar is contrasted against the always-non-negative A d squared term owned by parallel_axis_theorem_area, with the sign of the offset product carried through. Boundary recorded: area_moment_integral_definition owns the integral definition and supplies the machinery for a different integrand without being re-derived; parallel_axis_theorem_area and composite_area_moment_of_inertia are cited not re-derived; inclined_axis_area_moment and mohrs_circle_area_moment are excluded with no rotation, no angle of rotation and no graphical construction appearing anywhere; the parked conceptual sibling product_of_inertia is not encroached upon, this node being the computational one per the Architect ruling; no mass and no density, this being an area property. Symbol pre-check performed against all five signed moments-of-inertia siblings: A, A_i, x, y, dA and y_bar reused with identical meaning, I_xy, I_xy_c, x_bar, x_i and y_i introduced, and bare I and bare k deliberately not rebound. ordered_steps: Name the common origin and the original perpendicular x-y pair. Take I_x and I_y as given from area_moment_of_inertia and area_moment_integral_definition; take I_xy as given from product_of_inertia_area. Do not re-derive I_xy and do not re-establish its sign or symmetry properties. State that this skill transforms by ROTATION about that common origin: no axis is translated to a different point, so parallel_axis_theorem_area is not used. Do not integrate, assemble composites, construct Mohr's circle, or compute a principal angle or principal moment. No mass and no density.

Define the rotated u-v pair sharing the same origin. Measure theta from the original x-axis to the u-axis with a stated rotational sense and stated units (degrees or radians). Form the double angle 2theta; do not substitute theta where 2theta is required.
Form the intermediate sums once and reuse them: (I_x + I_y)/2 and (I_x - I_y)/2. These are terms of the transformation relations, not a centroid average.

Substitute into the three transformation relations, retaining the sign of I_xy and the opposing signs of the cos and I_xy terms between the I_u and I_v relations. Obtain I_u, I_v, and I_uv. Do not drop I_xy or assume it is zero when it is not. Rotation need not make I_uv zero.

Screen the dropped-product error when useful: recompute the three transformed values with I_xy wrongly taken as zero and note that every value changes while the sum invariant can still hold. That screen shows what the invariant does not catch.

Verify before reporting by the sum invariant: I_u + I_v must equal I_x + I_y. Agreement is an independent check on the pair taken together; it does not validate I_uv or the given inputs, and it cannot detect compensating shifts between I_u and I_v.

Report I_u, I_v, and I_uv with the named rotated pair, the stated theta, and length^4 units. Stop. Do not construct Mohr's circle, compute principal axes or principal moments, integrate, re-derive I_xy, or apply the parallel-axis theorem.

ordered_steps: State the ownership boundary in one sentence: inclined_axis_area_moment transforms area moments to a given orientation; this skill finds the principal orientation and extrema from Mohr's circle. Take I_x, I_y, and I_xy as given — do not re-derive them. Cite the signed transformation I_uv = ((I_x − I_y)/2) sin 2theta + I_xy cos 2theta only later when confirming I_uv = 0; do not re-derive it as the objective and do not reopen the signed inclined-axis procedure. No mass, no density, no parallel-axis translation.

Construct the circle from the known inputs: place the center at I_avg = (I_x + I_y)/2 on the horizontal I-axis and compute R = sqrt(((I_x − I_y)/2)^2 + I_xy^2). Retain the sign of I_xy. State that the deliverable is this center-radius construction, not a transformation at a pre-supplied angle.

Read the principal moments as the circle extrema: I_max = I_avg + R and I_min = I_avg − R. These are where the circle crosses the horizontal axis. Do not treat the reference x-y pair as already principal when I_xy is nonzero.

Determine the principal orientation under the project's signed convention: solve tan 2theta_p = −I_xy / ((I_x − I_y)/2) and select the branch that makes signed I_uv vanish. Obtain the physical angle as theta_p = (1/2)(2theta_p). State the doubling explicitly — 2theta_p is the circle angle; theta_p is the physical axis rotation. Do not report the circle angle as the physical rotation. Note that the unsigned reference formula tan 2theta_p = I_xy / ((I_x − I_y)/2) gives the same line of axes but its principal-value branch must be reconciled with the signed convention.

Verify before reporting. (1) Sum invariant: I_max + I_min must equal I_x + I_y. (2) Zero product: evaluate signed I_uv at 2theta_p and confirm it is zero; optionally show that the unsigned principal-value branch leaves I_uv nonzero. Record the honest limitation: the sum does not alone confirm R; the zero-product check relies on the cited transformation; neither validates the inputs.

Report I_max, I_min, physical theta_p, and circle 2theta_p, with mm^4 units and the named reference pair. Stop — do not apply a transformation at a supplied angle as a substitute for the circle construction.

signature.notes: Mohr's circle for area moments of inertia, the held position-3 node authored after the Architect ruling resolved principal-axis ownership to this skill. The physical-versus-circle doubling is exercised explicitly, 2theta_p = 135 degrees as the circle angle and theta_p = 67.5 degrees as the physical rotation, the factor of two named as the defining Mohr's-circle interpretation and required element (d) of the ruling. Two independent verifications: the sum invariant I_max + I_min = 14.0000 x 10^6 = I_x + I_y, and the zero-product check at the principal orientation. ordered_steps: State the area-versus-mass contrast prominently: area_moment_of_inertia / area_moment_integral_definition compute I = ∫ r² dA over AREA (dimension L⁴); this skill computes I = ∫ r² dm over MASS (dimension M L²) — same r² structure, different measure and dimension. Do not re-derive the area moment. Name in one sentence that the mass moment of inertia is the quantity that governs resistance to angular acceleration about the stated axis; do NOT author angular acceleration, kinetic energy, stress, or an equation of motion. Cite standard relations as given; do not derive them. The mass parallel-axis relation I = I_cm + m d² is the analogue of the area theorem (transfer A d²); state the analogy and USE the mass form — do not re-derive the area theorem. Exclude product_of_inertia_area, inclined_axis_area_moment, and Mohr's circle. No equilibrium equations.

For each mass element or point mass, form r (or r_i) as the PERPENDICULAR distance to the named axis — not the distance to a point or to the origin, except when the axis through the origin makes those distances coincide. A wrong length that is still a length is a placement error on r.

Select the named axis and the matching expression for r². For discrete point masses at coordinates (x, y): about the z-axis through the origin, r² = x² + y²; about the x-axis, r² = y². Compute I = Σ m_i r_i² for each required axis. Do not mix the r formula of one axis with another. Continuous bodies may also be integrated directly as ∫ r² dm when required.

When an approved standard relation is given for a common shape about a stated axis, substitute and evaluate (for example I_cm = (1/12) m L² for a slender rod about a perpendicular centre-of-mass axis). Transfer to a parallel axis with I = I_cm + m d² when required.

Verify before reporting. (1) Dimensional: every mass-moment result must be kg·m² — a result in m⁴ would signal the area-mass conflation; this check does not catch a wrong length that is still a length. (2) When both a transfer route and an independent tabulated relation are available for the same axis, confirm they agree. Record that each I is only about its stated axis.
Report each mass moment with the named axis and kg·m² units. Stop — do not author dynamics, do not compute an area moment, and do not derive a standard relation presented as given.
